questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is abstraction in computational thinking?
options: Hiding the details and focusing only on what's important
questions.answer: Hiding the details and focusing only on what's important
questions.hint: Think of a tube map — it doesn't show every street.
questions.explanation: Abstraction means removing unnecessary detail to focus on the important parts. A tube map is an abstraction — it ignores actual distances and streets to show the connections clearly.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is decomposition in computational thinking?
options: Breaking a big problem down into smaller, easier sub-problems
Combining many small programs into one
questions.answer: Breaking a big problem down into smaller, easier sub-problems
questions.hint: 'De-' means apart. You're breaking something apart.
questions.explanation: Decomposition means breaking a large problem into smaller, more manageable parts that are easier to solve individually.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is pattern recognition in computational thinking?
options: Spotting similarities or trends between problems
questions.answer: Spotting similarities or trends between problems
questions.hint: Patterns mean things that repeat or look similar.
questions.explanation: Pattern recognition is looking for similarities between problems. If you've solved a similar problem before, you can reuse the same approach.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is an algorithm?
options: A step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem
questions.answer: A step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem
questions.hint: A recipe is a real-world example.
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a step-by-step sequence of instructions that solves a problem. A recipe, directions to a friend's house, and a maths method are all algorithms.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT one of the four main ideas in computational thinking?
questions.answer: Encryption
questions.hint: Encryption is about security, not problem-solving.
questions.explanation: The four main computational thinking ideas are: decomposition, abstraction, pattern recognition and algorithmic thinking. Encryption is a security topic, not a CT pillar.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these is the BEST example of abstraction?
options: Listing every brick that makes up a house
A Google Map that shows only the roads you'll drive on, not every shop
Writing down every step a computer takes when starting up
Reading every line of code in a video game
questions.answer: A Google Map that shows only the roads you'll drive on, not every shop
questions.hint: Abstraction = removing detail you don't need.
questions.explanation: Google Maps abstracts away unnecessary detail (every shop, building, tree) and shows only what you need for navigation. That's the essence of abstraction.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Bertie wants to build a game where the player collects coins, avoids enemies and reaches a flag. Decomposition would suggest he should:
options: Write all the code in one massive function
Break the game into smaller parts: player movement, coin collection, enemies, level end
Just start coding without a plan
questions.answer: Break the game into smaller parts: player movement, coin collection, enemies, level end
questions.hint: Decomposition = breaking the big problem into smaller ones.
questions.explanation: Decomposition tackles big problems by splitting them into smaller, manageable pieces. Building each game system separately and combining them is much easier than tackling everything at once.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: When designing his game, Bertie notices that 'player', 'enemy' and 'coin' all need to know their x and y position on screen. What kind of computational thinking is this?
questions.answer: Pattern recognition
questions.hint: He's spotting that different things share the same features.
questions.explanation: He's spotting a shared pattern between three different things — they all need x and y positions. Recognising this means he can reuse the same approach for all of them.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is a flowchart used for?
options: Visually showing the steps and decisions in an algorithm
questions.answer: Visually showing the steps and decisions in an algorithm
questions.hint: It uses shapes and arrows.
questions.explanation: A flowchart uses shapes (rectangles for processes, diamonds for decisions, etc.) and arrows to show the steps of an algorithm visually.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is pseudocode?
options: An English-like way of writing an algorithm, not a real programming language
A code that only fake hackers use
questions.answer: An English-like way of writing an algorithm, not a real programming language
questions.hint: 'Pseudo' means 'pretend' or 'almost'.
questions.explanation: Pseudocode is a way of writing algorithms using plain English-style instructions. It's not a real programming language but is easy for humans to read and easy to translate into real code.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Put the following algorithm steps for making a cup of tea in the correct order.
options: Pour the boiling water into the cup
Add the tea bag to the cup
answer: Add the tea bag to the cup
Pour the boiling water into the cup
questions.hint: You can't pour water until it's boiled. You can't take the tea bag out until it's in there.
questions.explanation: Order matters in algorithms. Boil first, tea bag in, pour water, brew and remove bag, then milk last. Each step depends on the previous.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these is a SEQUENCE in programming?
options: A series of instructions carried out one after another
Repeating the same thing many times
questions.answer: A series of instructions carried out one after another
questions.hint: 'Sequence' means one thing follows another.
questions.explanation: Sequence is one of the three basic programming constructs — running instructions in order, one after the other. The others are selection (if/else) and iteration (loops).

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these is an example of SELECTION in programming?
options: if score > 10 then print('Win') else print('Try again')
questions.answer: if score > 10 then print('Win') else print('Try again')
questions.hint: Selection = choosing one path or another. Look for 'if'.
questions.explanation: Selection means choosing which code to run based on a condition. An if/else statement is the classic example.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these is an example of ITERATION (a loop)?
questions.answer: for i in range(10): print(i)
questions.hint: Iteration = repeating something. Look for 'for' or 'while'.
questions.explanation: Iteration means repeating instructions. 'for' and 'while' loops are the two main types of iteration.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What name is given to a part of a program that repeats a block of code? (One word)
questions.answer: loop
questions.hint: It goes round and round.
questions.explanation: A loop repeats a block of code. The two main kinds are 'for' loops (run a set number of times) and 'while' loops (run until a condition is false).

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is a variable in programming?
options: A constant value that never changes
A named storage location that holds a value which can change
questions.answer: A named storage location that holds a value which can change
questions.hint: It can vary — the value can change.
questions.explanation: A variable is a labelled box in memory that stores a value. The value can change as the program runs. Example: score = 0, then later score = 5.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What does IDE stand for?
questions.answer: Integrated Development Environment
questions.hint: It's software programmers use to write and test code.
questions.explanation: IDE stands for Integrated Development Environment — software that combines a code editor, a way to run code, and tools to help find bugs (like IDLE, VS Code, PyCharm).

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these are typical features of an IDE? (Select all that apply)
options: A code editor with syntax highlighting
A way to run your code
A debugger to help find errors
answer: A code editor with syntax highlighting
A way to run your code
A debugger to help find errors
questions.hint: Anything that helps you WRITE, RUN or FIX code.
questions.explanation: IDEs bundle together everything a programmer needs: editor, runner, debugger, autocomplete. Printers and vacuum cleaners are not part of an IDE.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is the name for an error in a program? (One word, four letters)
questions.answer: bug
questions.hint: Famous story: a real moth was found in an early computer.
questions.explanation: A bug is an error in a program. The process of finding and fixing bugs is called debugging.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is a SYNTAX error?
options: The program runs but gives the wrong answer
The code breaks the rules of the language and won't run (e.g. missing bracket)
questions.answer: The code breaks the rules of the language and won't run (e.g. missing bracket)
questions.hint: Syntax = the grammar rules of the language.
questions.explanation: A syntax error means the code breaks the language's grammar rules — like a missing colon, bracket or quote. The code won't run until it's fixed.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is a LOGIC error?
options: The code runs but produces the wrong result
questions.answer: The code runs but produces the wrong result
questions.hint: It runs fine — but the answer is wrong.
questions.explanation: A logic error means the code runs (no syntax problems) but doesn't do what was intended — e.g. using + instead of - in a calculation. These are harder to find than syntax errors.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Put these steps of a 'search a list of names for Bertie' algorithm in order.
options: Look at the next name in the list
If it matches 'Bertie', stop. Otherwise, move on
If the list ends with no match, report 'Not found'
answer: Look at the next name in the list
If it matches 'Bertie', stop. Otherwise, move on
If the list ends with no match, report 'Not found'
questions.hint: You must start somewhere, then check each item, deciding what to do as you go.
questions.explanation: This is a linear search: start at the first item, check each one in turn, stop with 'Found' on a match, or 'Not found' if you reach the end.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which is the BEST description of how abstraction and decomposition work together?
options: Decomposition splits the problem into parts; abstraction focuses on the important details of each part
Abstraction makes things bigger; decomposition makes things smaller
questions.answer: Decomposition splits the problem into parts; abstraction focuses on the important details of each part
questions.hint: Decomposition = break apart. Abstraction = ignore irrelevant detail.
questions.explanation: They are different but complementary. Decomposition breaks the problem into smaller sub-problems; abstraction strips away unimportant detail so you can focus on what matters in each one.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: A program is supposed to print the numbers 1 to 5, but it prints nothing. The line says 'for i in range(0): print(i)'. What kind of error is this?
options: Logic error — code runs but gives the wrong output
questions.answer: Logic error — code runs but gives the wrong output
questions.hint: Does the code run? Then is the output what was wanted?
questions.explanation: The code runs fine — it just loops 0 times because range(0) is empty. That's a logic error: the program does the wrong thing, but the code is grammatically valid.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: A student is solving lots of different word problems and notices they all involve 'finding the total of a list of numbers'. What computational thinking skill is this?
questions.answer: Pattern recognition
questions.hint: They've spotted the same kind of problem appearing in different disguises.
questions.explanation: Spotting that several problems share the same underlying structure ('total of a list') is pattern recognition. The same algorithm can then be reused for all of them.
